about: Where a trade happens and what it costs. One entry per venue; the engine reads every rule from here. Figures come from docs/library/money/2026-10-09-research-*.md; anything marked as an assumption is a placeholder because the real figure could not be read.

cfd.label: CFD broker (Plus500-style)
cfd.summary: Contracts for difference: you bet on the price with borrowed exposure. You never own the asset; you pay the spread on every trade and interest every night a trade stays open.
notes: Leverage caps are ASIC's retail limits (30:1 major currencies down to 2:1 crypto).

Overnight funding = the benchmark rate of the day + 3.0% a year on the full position value, charged every calendar night (a weekend counts three). Benchmark history: the RBA cash rate target (table A2) for AUD markets, the US 13-week T-bill rate (^IRX) for USD ones; 4.60% and 4.04% today. A currency pair pays on the gap between its two rates instead: a long AUD/USD pays the markup plus the US rate minus the Australian one, a short the markup plus the Australian rate minus the US one. The 3.0% markup is an assumption: Plus500's own rates could not be read.
Shorts receive the benchmark rate minus 3.0% (they pay when that is negative).
Spreads are from review sites and search summaries, several are assumptions (ASX 200, NASDAQ-100, AUD/USD, BHP). Real spreads widen in fast markets and outside main hours.
Profit or loss on a market priced in another currency pays a 0.7% conversion fee.
Margin close-out at 50% of the initial margin; negative balance protection floors the account at zero.
No interest on idle cash. Not modelled: the USD 10 a month inactivity fee after 3 idle months, guaranteed-stop fees, futures roll spreads.

sources.label: Plus500AU Financial Services Guide v21 (4 June 2026): no commission, 0.7% conversion fee, no interest on cash, funding x3 on Fridays
ASIC 20-254MR: retail CFD leverage caps, margin close-out, negative balance protection
RBA table A2, every cash rate target change (4.60% from 30 Sep 2026)

cash.label: Share broker ($3 a trade)
cash.summary: You buy and own real ETF units or shares (Stake or Moomoo style). No leverage, no shorting, a small fee per trade.
notes: Brokerage: A$3 or 0.03% of the trade, whichever is more (Moomoo's published price; Stake is A$3 too).
Buys wait until there is A$500 to spend: about the ASX's minimum first parcel, and it keeps the A$3 fee at 0.6% of the buy or less. Assumption on the exact rule.
Bid-ask spread 0.05% on large ETFs and shares: an assumption, not researched.
Buying US shares converts AUD to USD at a 0.5% fee: an assumption, not researched.

Idle cash earns the RBA cash rate of the day, as a high-interest savings account roughly does (5.00% today against a 4.60% cash rate). With no rate history it earns the fixed 2.5% (between the 10-year and 5-year averages to June 2026, Vanguard index chart).
Fund fees (0.04% to 0.27% a year) are already inside ETF prices, so they are not charged again.
